content.user_title: Map BMAD Work to Verified Evidence
content.value_statement: BMAD work can lose traceability between requirements, reviews, tests, and closure decisions. This skill maps BMAD artifacts to RVTF records while preserving host ownership, evidence quality, and review boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Maps BMAD Epics, Specs, Stories, and direct changes to RVTF goals, milestones, and units.
Connects acceptance criteria to requirements, journeys, verification methods, and evidence records.
Preserves review coverage, finding identity, triage status, and controlled reopen decisions.
Directs users to separate host status from RVTF closure and challenge unsupported completion claims.
Provides a BMAD review prompt for finding missing evidence, untraced scope, and lost gaps.
Supplies a compact YAML attachment shape for requirement, acceptance, journey, and step IDs.
limitations: It provides governance guidance and mappings, not an implementation of the RVTF system.
It does not execute BMAD builds, stories, tests, reviews, or orchestrator actions.
The mapping is pinned to the documented BMAD host revision and needs re-audit after host changes.
It cannot prove runtime behavior when execution evidence is missing.

use_cases.title: Plan Story Verification
use_cases.description: Map a BMAD Story and its acceptance criteria to RVTF requirements, journeys, verification methods, and evidence targets before implementation.

use_cases.title: Audit Review Coverage
use_cases.description: Check whether adversarial, edge-case, and verification-gap reviews preserve finding identity, required roles, evidence, and host triage decisions.

use_cases.title: Assess Epic Closure
use_cases.description: Evaluate a BMAD retrospective using declared criteria, Story status, revisions, runtime evidence, gaps, and the RVTF completion gate.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Trace Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this BMAD Story to RVTF requirements, acceptance items, journeys, and journey steps. Identify missing IDs and evidence targets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a traceability outline for one Story.

prompt_templates.title: Review Acceptance Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Story acceptance evidence. Separate item evidence from path evidence, identify unsupported claims, and list the smallest verification gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess whether completed work proves its acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge Review Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this BMAD review record for untraced scope, unsupported verified claims, missing review-batch coverage, lost deferred gaps, and unauthorized remediation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform an adversarial governance review.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Closure Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Epic or direct change against RVTF closure rules. Preserve host status, distinguish proposed actions from approved work, and report evidence gaps and required owner decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: produce a closure-readiness assessment without granting implementation authority.

output_examples.input: A Story has passing tests but no journey-step evidence.
output_examples.output: The tests may support acceptance-item evidence, but journey coverage remains unproven. Record a verification gap and narrow the closure claim.

output_examples.input: A retrospective proposes fixes for an unfinished Story.
output_examples.output: Keep the Story unfinished and the machine verdict rejected. Treat the fixes as proposals until an authorized owner routes them.

output_examples.input: A direct change has no resolved Story key.
output_examples.output: Map the actual change to one RVTF Unit. Do not update arbitrary sprint status or invent Story ownership.

best_practices: Use the actual closure boundary when mapping BMAD artifacts to RVTF scopes.
Keep host status, RVTF closure, evidence validity, and current test claims separate.
Preserve finding identity and review history before grouping surviving findings.
anti_patterns: Do not treat Story completion, Build completion, or retrospective completion as proof of RVTF closure.
Do not reuse evidence to remove mandatory host gates or claim current tests pass.
Do not convert deferred findings or advisory remediation into authorized work.

faq.question: What does this skill connect?
faq.answer: It connects BMAD scopes and lifecycle records to RVTF requirements, acceptance items, journeys, evidence, reviews, gaps, and closure rules.

faq.question: Does it run BMAD commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides mapping and review guidance. It does not invoke builds, stories, tests, reviews, or orchestrator actions.

faq.question: Can a Story prove RVTF closure?
faq.answer: No. Story completion remains host status. RVTF closure requires trace evidence and its own completion gate.

faq.question: How should direct changes be mapped?
faq.answer: Map one actual direct change to an appropriate RVTF Unit. Do not fabricate Story ownership or update sprint status without a real Story key.

faq.question: What evidence does review require?
faq.answer: Review should preserve finding identity, verify claimed consequences, record required roles, and distinguish item evidence from journey path evidence.

faq.question: When should this mapping be re-audited?
faq.answer: Re-audit it whenever BMAD Story, Build, review, triage, or orchestrator behavior changes from the pinned host revision.
